subject: phoenix
reasoning:
I'm planning a phoenix model with the SDK, aiming for an ambitious but safe design using simple, reliable calls—a standing bird with spread wings, long tail feathers, a crest, a beaked head, and legs, roughly 1.2m tall, starting with the root coordinates.

Defining body chains and sweeps...

Still working out beak geometry...

For the eyes, I need to place them symmetrically on either side of the head, so I'll write a small helper that flips left/right based on sign, then add white sphere eyes with dark pupils and a gold tint.

Now I'm adding plume-like spikes sweeping back from the head using bezier curves for a natural curve, then moving on to the wings, which spread outward from the shoulders with a simple arm chain down to the elbow and wrist.

Still designing feather extrusion...

Defining feather layers now, laying out nine primaries with increasing sweep angles and lengths, and setting up a color gradient from red through orange to gold at the tips...

Still refining feather attachment logic...

Still writing tail feather geometry...

Setting up the leg chains with digitigrade bends across three segments, naming the joints hip/knee/ankle/foot, and sweeping them with a thin gold-ish profile.

Now I'm shaping the toes as spikes off each foot point—three forward and one back—tapering their radius from base to tip so they sit low and slightly sunk near the ground plane.

Tweaking feather shapes for the scatter...

I'm also considering adding a golden collar sweep around the neck joint and a tapered body sweep along the spine with varying radii at each point.

Working out the body path curve and neck sweep with its own radii, shaping an S-curve from the body up to the head position.

For the crest, I'm defining a bezier curve relative to the head joint, with a small helper to handle left/right offsets safely instead of risking negative values. Then I'll move on to posing the wings spread with added coverts.

Now I'm setting up a wing arm chain per side, parented to the last spine joint, swept along a curved path, plus a feather helper function that builds extruded feather shapes with position, orientation, thickness, and color based on length and width parameters.

I'll switch to using arm.nearestJoint directly, skip bevel for simplicity, and use a paint closure that colors along the outline. Each feather layer gets a distinct lift to avoid z-fighting, with primaries drooping slightly and coverts added as a row of shorter feathers along the arm.

Now I'm laying out the covert feathers with varying angles and lifts in orange/gold tones, then setting up the hip joint, spine chain, and tail chain with catmull-spline positions, attaching tail feathers to the tail bone near the base.
